Weights Saturday, August 15. High weights preferred. In the event in the race overfills, horses with equal weights (adjusted for age) will receive equal draw. The Green Flash Handicap has been selected as one of the Breeders' Cup "Win and You're In" Challenge Races. The nominated winner of the Green Flash Handicap will be entitled to automatic entry into the 2026 running of the Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint. The nominated winner will also be entitled to have pre-entry and entry fees waived for the Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint or will receive a credit equal to the Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint per-entry and entry fee amount towards any other Breeders' Cup Championship Race and will be entitled to receive a travel stipend if traveling from a base located outside California. To be eligible for the 2026 Breeders' Cup World Championships to be held at Keeneland on October 30 and October 31, 2026, all horses must be pre-entered by noon (local standard time at the designated pre-entry locations) by Monday, October 19, 2026. Winner must be Breeders' Cup nominated by pre-entry deadline to receive Challenge rewards. All Breeders' Cup Challenge Races and Breeders' Cup World Championship races are to be run Lasix free in accordance with Breeders' Cup Limited rules as they may be published and/or amended from time to time, which rules are hereby expressly incorporated by this reference. All runners nominated to Challenge races and all Challenge winners are subject to out-of-competition testing by HIWU on behalf of HISA (or their respective designees). Breeders' Cup Limited reserves the right in its sole discretion to postpone, discontinue, amend, or change the conditions of all or any part of the Breeders' Cup Challenge "Win & You're In" race program. A trophy will be presented to Five Furlongs. (Turf)(Rail at 0 Feet) the winning owner.

analysis.text: A decent runner-up finish by BORN TO ROCK makes him the choice in this maiden-50 turf mile. 'ROCK was dropping from MSW to maiden-50, ran his final five-sixteenths in a solid :29.26, and missed by only a half-length. Likely winner if he runs two alike. PLETTENBERG BAY finished a head behind the top choice while racing for the first time in six months. Solid comeback by 'BAY, who has a right to improve second start back. If there is a knock on the last race by the top pair, it is that heav- ily favored Timayyyy was badly compromised by an equipment malfunction. He finished fourth. The top pair took advantage of the favorite's misfire, both ran well. FLAMBOYANT drops to maiden-50 after finishing unplaced in five successive MSW races. The speed figures earned by late-runner FLAMBOYANT compare favorably to the top choices. BOGARTS BUCCHERO drops in class and stretches out as a pace factor. From the rail, 'BUCCHERO is likely to produce speed.

A maiden facing winners, front-runner MY GIRL MIA is the choice to wire this non-winners of two $12.5k claiming sprint. 'MIA set the pace to near the eighth pole last time before she faded to fourth. That race was an auction race at six and one-half furlongs, now she cuts back to five and a half as the one to catch. Last-out maiden- 16 winner COTTA RIDE would benefit if the speed backs up. 'RIDE won rallying from behind, she clearly likes the Del Mar surface with a win and a second from two starts here. Claimed by Mark Glatt, 'RIDE could get a favorable trip forwardly placed just off the speed, in front of the deep closers. SHADY STRIPES set the pace and tired last out at six and a half; she also benefits by the turnback to five and one-half. 'STRIPES is the main pace threat for the top choice. The filly who beat 'STRIPES last out (Pretty Cecy) returned to finish a second against better on Sunday.

The longshot KING OF DRAGONS is worth backing in this Cal-bred allowance turf route that sets up for his closing style. His last-out fifth-place finish was better than it looks. Last early, he uncorked a premature move, got hung wide while rally- ing on the far turn and into the stretch, then flattened out. Good race, actually. He switches jockeys after the bad trip, gets pace to flatter his closing kick, and can post a come-from-behind upset in a race with speed to run at. The front-runners include TRUMP ERA , who ran super when second last out. That was the same race in which 'DRAGONS finished fifth. The horse who defeated TRUMP ERA by a half- length returned Saturday to win an open N1X. The challenge for TRUMP ERA is pace; he must cope with other speeds including STYLISHLYACCLAIMED . The latter has not raced in more than three months (vet scratch July 25), but he runs well fresh and won a maiden race over the DMR turf two years ago returning from a layoff. 'ACCLAIMED has speed, but does not require the lead. FEELING LUCKY has speed, and so does NAFTIS. Another late-runner worth considering is SOGNO DI VINO. Wide-open race, actually. SATURDAY, AUGUST 22, 2026 BEST BET: RACE 9, KENSINGTON LANE Del Mar Bottom Line By Brad Free Brad Free has been handicapper, reporter and columnist for Daily Racing Form since 1992. A native of Southern California, Free previously covered horse racing for the Pasadena Star- News, The National and The Racing Times. Free wrote the popular DRF text “Handicapping 101,” worked as a broadcaster for TVG and Santa Anita, and has served as track linemaker. 8 9 Del Mar Bottom Line

Two-year-old maidens at a mile on dirt; a pair of million-dollar first-time starters are the choices. MOTGA , purchased for $1.05 million this spring, makes his debut with a string of steady works for Bob Baffert. Tough to win a route first time out, of course. The past five years, Baffert is 5-for-28 with all two-turn first-time starters. PSALM was purchased as a yearling for $1.25 million and will make his debut for trainer Michael McCarthy. A full brother to G2 Remsen winner (and debut winner) Maximus Mischief, PSALM looked second-best in both recent half-mile works, but his pedigree suggests two turns will be his deal. McCarthy is 8-for-96 with two-turn first-time starters (all ages, all surfaces) the past five years. Due to their inexperience, the top two are not particularly reliable. TAKE A PICTURE has a race under his belt, an okay third in his debut at Ellis Park. That race has not been productive, however.

MOTORIOUS seeks his fourth victory in the G2 Green Flash. The veteran 8yo ran well finishing second in his allowance comeback last month, which was his first start in more than six months. This stakes race was always his summer target; MOTORIOUS was using the allowance as a prep for this. He is likely to improve second start back over a turf-sprint course on which he has four wins. He will rally from behind, as will 7yo SUMTER , who upset the top choice last out. SUMTER has maintained excellent form all year, and is a better horse than he was a year ago when he finished eighth in this race. SORRENTO SKY , stablemate of MOTORIOUS, looms the upset candidate. 'SKY was a first-time gelding last out when he finished a length behind SUMTER. Although 'SKY rallied from last in the comeback, he is likely to be more forwardly placed second start back. His connections believe he has improved since he became a “G.”

SEA'S NO JOKE and FURIOSITY , 2-year-old debut fillies trained by Baffert, look ready to fire. SEA'S NO JOKE looked good on video in her final workout; juve- nile progeny of Practical Joke have won at a 14 percent rate first out. FURIOSITY worked in company Aug. 2 with Miss Monica, who exited the workout to win her debut by more than five lengths with an 87 Beyer. FURIOSITY, who was second- best in the work with Miss Monica, came back with a sharp five-furlong gate drill Aug. 13. She is ready to fire; juvenile progeny of Into Mischief have won at a 15 percent rate first time out. The Baffert stablemates look evenly matched. Also-el- igible THEBEACHISBACK ran better than the line looks in her debut in an auction race. She broke slowly, was rushed, fanned five-wide into the stretch, and finished okay. She is facing tougher here, but has an experience edge over the top two.

The longshot AMERICAN HOPE can upset this N2X turf mile that has plenty of speed to flatter his closing rally. Since stretching back out this year, 'HOPE has improved (win, third, better-than-looked seventh). His last-start seventh in the Wickerr Stakes was better than it looks. The race was dominated by speed, 'HOPE lost ground while rallying wide, and ran his final quarter-mile in :22.39 to miss by only three lengths. FIRST PEACE finished fifth in the same stakes the top choice exits. This is the first allowance race that FIRST PEACE has contested since 2024; he figures for a tucked-in trip right behind the speed while entered for the $100k optional claim tag and facing easier. CHARLIE'S TO BLAME fits off back-to-back runner-up finishes at this N2X level. However, the pace scenario is a challenge for the front-runner/pace-presser. MAGNIFY can make amends for finishing third as the N1X favorite last out; he gets the call to even the score against one-two finishers NATIVE LAND and PURE MADNESS . The loss by MAGNIFY last out was partly due to the race shape. The 1-2-4 finishers were forwardly placed; MAGNIFY ran against the grain. He rallied from last to finish third. This field has even more speed, which could set up his closing rally. NATIVE LAND virtually wired the race in which the top choice finished third. 'LAND dueled through a hot pace and refused to surrender. He earned the highest Beyer of his career (94), runs back at the same level while entered for the optional $50k claim tag, and will be forwardly placed again. PURE MADNESS finished second in the same race, it was only his second start of the season. The lightly raced 5yo has never run a bad race (three wins, three seconds from six starts).

KENSINGTON LANE enters the G1 Del Mar Oaks as the class of the field. G1 winner last month at Saratoga in her U.S. debut; she was a notch below the top 3yo fillies in Europe, where she won a G3. Transferred to California soon after her front-running win at SAR, she has trained well at DMR. Her up-front style suits this nine-furlong turf stakes that is light on pace. VICTORIOUS DREAM looms as an upset candidate. Vastly improved this season, each recent start has been better than the start before including an emphatic N1X win last out. It's a big class hike to G1, but trainer Michael McCarthy upset this G1 last year with last-out N1X winner Velocity. Same pattern this year. RAIDING PARTY had a bad trip last month when third in the G2 San Clemente. She broke from the rail, but somehow ended up on the far outside, losing ground while rallying wide on the far turn and into the lane. She finished third in a race that was much better than it looks. She drew a tough post this time (10 of 10), but her trip cannot be any worse than last out.

Lots of questions and shippers in the G1 Pacific Classic including KNIGHTSBRIDGE from the East Coast. He is the fastest in the field on figures (122 Beyer last out), but racing a mile and a quarter for the first time while facing a host of other speed. KNIGHTSBRIDGE has run well from off the pace, and from post 11 may have the opportunity to establish position into the first turn either setting or pressing in the clear. If the fastest horse stays the distance, it's over with a forwardly placed trip. NAVAJO WARRIOR also ships from the East; he moves up in class following a pair of facile G3 wins that earned triple-digit figures. Although he won both races setting the pace, he is effective rallying from just off behind. That is key, because this year's Pacific Classic is loaded with speed. SUBSANADOR , G1 winner two years ago, had a shoe malfunction that was partly responsible for his last-start misfire in a G2. He has worked very well for his comeback; his closing style suits the pace scenario. OM N JOY, a filly facing colts and geldings, appears to be in tough. But her off-the-pace style could be beneficial in a race with pace-collapse potential.

KING OF GOSFORD moves back up in class into the G2 Del Mar Mile, after a confi- dence-building win in a restricted stake. 'GOSFORD won a G1 last year at SA, and has returned to top form this year at age 5. His versatility allows him to set the pace or rally from behind. No reason he cannot score right back. DETAIN also moves up, following a N2X win that was only his second start in the U.S. He was Group 1-placed in Europe and will be rolling late. EL POTENTE is stuck in the outside post (12 of 12), but he has been working well for his comeback. Expect him to produce speed, along with CABO SPIRIT.
